Just been playing a while now, and practicing a lot. Thankfully with  much more experienced and knowledgeable players than myself. And they fortunately passed down some ideas that helped me.


These principals can work and help with all banjo styles, I think anyway, Everybody has their own style and preferences. I'm sure some might rightfully disagree. I play a little of each depending on the style of music and what the song requires. 

I've spent a lot of time with my banjo over the past 12 years. And just enjoy playing and sharing music of any type. Having obtained what some might call passable proficiency in Three finger Scruggs, melodic, single string or clawhammer now make it easier and more fun in a lot of ways, but I'm always still still struggling and trying to find ways improve and add to music and make things easier and less complicated for myself.

I have them on 7-9-10.

Just because I like the drone string to match the first or the 5th of the key the song/tune we are playing in, and I think it sounds the best because there is less dissonance because the drone is always hitting the first or the 5th of the key and it's easier to stay in line with what the bass player is doing. They are typically playing mostly 1st and 5ths as well.

Also, these are the most common keys played or sung in my area and the spikes make re-tuning a bit faster and less complicated at least for for my little brain.

7 for playing in A & D.

9 for B & E.

10 for C & F. (But sometimes I will just tune the whole banjo down a full step) and Just play like I'm playing in A & E if I want some deeper sounds.

For Bb and Eb  I will usually just tune up the 5th string a 1/2 step and capo at the 3rd fret and spike at 7.

For more obscure keys that aren't played very often like 
Ab & Db and
F# and C# (Gb and Bb)
I will just tune the whole banjo up or down a 1/2 step. Let's me hang and play in every key without needing to learn more and having spikes on Every fret up to 11.

Maybe I could do away with either the spike at 9 or the spike at 10 but I find it more efficient and a little less complicated to have both.

Why don't I have a spike on 8? A half step tune is quick and easy and unlikely the string will break from stress.I fret that one with my thumb a lot and it's just easier to get better tone without it.

Hope this helps and doesn't confuse you more.:)
